args.title: Dedupe collapses legitimate same-day, same-amount transactions
args.body:
File: src/ingest/dedupe.ts

dedupeKey() only uses date, amount, and description, so two genuinely separate transactions with the same date/amount/description (e.g. two identical coffees bought the same morning) are indistinguishable from a true duplicate row caused by an overlapping statement upload, and the second one is silently dropped. The key should account for the occurrence count/position of matching rows within a single file (or statement) so that repeated identical rows are preserved unless they come from an overlapping upload, rather than being treated purely as duplicates by content alone.

file: src/ingest/dedupe.ts
This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

This is a real data-loss bug rather than intended behaviour. dedupeKey() builds its key purely from date + amount + description (see src/ingest/dedupe.ts), with no notion of row position or occurrence count. That works for the overlapping-statement case it was designed for (the same row appearing in two uploads), but it also wrongly collapses two genuinely separate transactions that happen to share date, amount, and description within the same file or statement — exactly your two coffees. The fix should let repeated identical rows within one upload survive, while still catching true duplicates from overlapping statements.
